answer: Artificial intelligence, or AI, is the field of building computer systems that do tasks which normally need human thinking [01-001].

Machine learning is one way of building AI [02-001]. Instead of a programmer writing every rule by hand, the system learns patterns from examples [02-001]. It is an approach that depends on learning from data [02-003].
Overfitting is when a system performs well on training data but poorly on test data because it has memorised the examples rather than learning a general pattern [03-002].

The quality of training examples matters because if the examples are few, unbalanced, or wrong, the system learns the wrong patterns [02-004].
A system trained on sunny photos might fail on night photos because it learns the patterns it sees rather than the patterns intended by the people building it [03-003].

An AI system can be fair in some cases and unfair in others, depending on how it was built and tested [06-002]. AI systems learn from data, and if the data contains gaps or bias, the system can repeat those problems in its answers [06-002].

An AI answer can sound confident and still be wrong because fluency is not the same as accuracy [07-001]. Additionally, AI tools built from narrow or biased data tend to give narrow or biased answers even when their wording sounds confident [03-004].
